title: Native Windows OpenCode reversible system bootstrap
intent: Converge a Windows x64 workstation onto an official machine-wide OpenCode CLI plus admin-managed lsp=true configuration, while durably recording ownership so every ASB-owned machine mutation can be reversed without deleting unrelated state.

ascertainBeforeMutation: 64-bit architecture and AMD64 for this first implementation
administrator elevation for Apply and Remove
existing durable AgentSwitchboard OpenCode lifecycle state

lifecycle.interruptedApplyRecovery: a pending binary/PATH/config mutation is recovered only when observed state matches either the recorded baseline or the exact planned ASB state; any third state fails closed

managedConfiguration.removeRollback: property-level three-way rollback of only lsp and $schema when those properties were changed by ASB; unrelated later properties are preserved

remove.binary: delete only an ASB-created binary or restore a verified preexisting binary backup; current binary SHA-256 must equal recorded post-Apply hash before rollback
remove.installDirectory: remove only when ASB created the directory and it is empty after owned binary rollback
remove.machinePath: remove only the exact installDirectory entry when durable state records addedByAsb=true
remove.managedConfig: restore only ASB-changed properties to their recorded pre-ASB presence/value; preserve unrelated properties; fail closed on drift

powershellSafety.reason: PowerShell parses the complete .ps1 before execution, preventing a separately submitted else block or other split control-flow fragment from being treated as a new command.

forbidden: overwriting malformed or JSONC managed configuration
blind recursive deletion of Program Files or ProgramData roots
removing a PATH entry that predates ASB ownership
restoring a whole shared config file over unrelated later edits
silently re-baselining an owned resource after outside drift
restarting Remove from scratch after a durably checkpointed partial rollback
deleting OpenCode user credentials, sessions, project state, caches, or unrelated settings
claiming lsp=true alone proves an active language server
claiming Remove succeeded without verifying rollback
